notable_absence.finding: This page states 'Has 3 modes of operation: `no_cas`, `bad_cas`, and `good_cas`' - the identical no_cas/bad_cas/good_cas test harness that this same batch's advancedDeleteOp.md documents (plus a 4th no_key mode). Round 8's Capella twin modeled DeleteOp's version of this harness as a distinct concept, eventing:cas-conditioned-delete, but left this REPLACE page's structurally identical harness unmodeled (empty concepts/relations, reasoning that it is 'standard Data Service optimistic-concurrency (CAS) behavior... not an Eventing-specific mechanism'). This record keeps that same call for consistency, but flags the asymmetry explicitly below (cross_component_finding) since the same reasoning, applied evenly, would either mint both or neither.

cross_component_finding: advancedReplaceOp.md and advancedDeleteOp.md document the same CAS-conditioned-write test harness (no_cas always succeeds / bad_cas always fails with LCB_KEY_EEXISTS,cas_mismatch:true / good_cas succeeds after reading the current CAS via couchbase.get) against two different Advanced Accessor operations (replace vs delete; delete additionally has a no_key mode). Only the DELETE version was modeled as a distinct concept in round 8 (eventing:cas-conditioned-delete) - the REPLACE version, despite being evidenced by nearly the same sentence ('Has 3 modes of operation: `no_cas`, `bad_cas`, and `good_cas`' here vs 'Has 4 modes of operation: ...' on DeleteOp), was left conceptually unmodeled. Worth reconciliation considering whether eventing:cas-conditioned-delete's scope should generalize to a shared eventing:cas-conditioned-write concept covering both REPLACE and DELETE, rather than being named for one operation only.
